headline: Ex-IGP Benazir Ahmed released from Dubai jail amid unconfirmed reports
summary: Former Police Chief Benazir Ahmed reportedly left prison on Thursday, though Bangladesh Police and the ACC have yet to receive official confirmation.
details: Reports indicate that former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed has been released from a prison in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. While close sources claim he left prison last Thursday, Bangladesh Police and the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) have not yet officially confirmed the news.

The Bangladesh Police headquarters is attempting to establish official contact with Dubai authorities, but communication has been delayed due to a public holiday in the UAE. A spokesperson for the police headquarters stated that they have received no official notification regarding his release.

Benazir Ahmed was arrested in Dubai with the help of Interpol following a case filed by the ACC. He had left the country after the fall of the previous government, following investigations into his and his family's vast assets.

The ACC has filed four separate cases against Benazir, his wife Jishan Mirza, and two daughters for the illegally acquired assets. The total amount of illegal wealth, totaling 74 crore BDT, including land, flats, and company shares, has been attached by court order.
Benazir Ahmed served as the IGP from April 2020 to September 2022. He also previously served as the DMP Commissioner and the Director General of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).
In December 2021, the United States imposed sanctions on Benazir Ahmed and six other RAB officials for serious human rights violations.
caption:
Is former IGP Benazir Ahmed free? Reports suggest he has been released from a Dubai jail, but official confirmation is pending.

Reports indicate that former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed has been released from a prison in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. While close sources claim he left prison last Thursday, Bangladesh Police and the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) have not yet officially confirmed the news.

The Bangladesh Police headquarters is attempting to establish official contact with Dubai authorities, but communication has been delayed due to a public holiday in the UAE. A spokesperson for the police headquarters stated that they have received no official notification regarding his release.

Benazir Ahmed was arrested in Dubai with the help of Interpol following a case filed by the ACC. He had left the country after the fall of the previous government, following investigations into his and his family's vast assets.

The ACC has filed four separate cases against Benazir, his wife Jishan Mirza, and two daughters for the illegally acquired assets. The total amount of illegal wealth, totaling 74 crore BDT, including land, flats, and company shares, has been attached by court order.

Benazir Ahmed served as the IGP from April 2020 to September 2022. He also previously served as the DMP Commissioner and the Director General of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).

In December 2021, the United States imposed sanctions on Benazir Ahmed and six other RAB officials for serious human rights violations.

headline: Tk70 hike: 12kg LPG cylinder price rises to Tk1,598 for August
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the price of 12kg LPG cylinders for the month of August.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the price of 12kg liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders by Tk70.
As a result, the new consumer-level price for a 12kg cylinder has been set at Tk1,598, including VAT.
The price hike was announced in a notice issued by BERC on Sunday, August 2.
The new pricing is effective from 6:00 PM on Sunday evening.
According to BERC, the new price will remain in effect until further notice.
caption:
LPG prices are up. A 12kg cylinder now costs Tk1,598 after a Tk70 increase.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has increased the price of 12kg liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders by Tk70.

As a result, the new consumer-level price for a 12kg cylinder has been set at Tk1,598, including VAT.

The price hike was announced in a notice issued by BERC on Sunday, August 2.

The new pricing is effective from 6:00 PM on Sunday evening.

According to BERC, the new price will remain in effect until further notice.
